question: In an emergency, how may riders be allowed to exit a bus, according to the Connecticut CDL manual?
choice_a: By any window or door
choice_b: Only through the main entry door
choice_c: Only through a designated rear emergency exit
choice_d: Only after the driver manually releases each window
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to allow riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency, since a normal exit path may be blocked or unsafe.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: What must shippers do to containers of hazardous material, according to the rules described in the manual?
choice_a: Mark them with the material's name, identification number, and hazard label
choice_b: Mark them only with a general warning color code
choice_c: Seal them in a locked hazmat container
choice_d: Attach a bill of lading listing the driver's name
explanation: The manual states the rules require shippers to mark containers of hazardous material with the material's name, identification number, and hazard label.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Besides emergency hospital supplies and drugs, what type of ammunition may a bus carry?
choice_a: Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D
choice_b: Any ammunition labeled as a Class 1 explosive
choice_c: Any ammunition weighing under 100 pounds
choice_d: Only blank or training ammunition
explanation: The manual states buses may carry small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Which of the following must a bus NEVER carry, according to the Connecticut CDL manual?
choice_a: Division 2.3 poison gas, liquid Class 6 poison, tear gas, or irritating material
choice_b: Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D
choice_c: Emergency hospital supplies
choice_d: Up to 100 pounds of any one allowed hazardous materials class
explanation: The manual explicitly forbids buses from carrying Division 2.3 poison gas, liquid Class 6 poison, tear gas, or irritating material.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Under what circumstance are explosives permitted in the space occupied by riders on a bus?
choice_a: Only if they are small arms ammunition
choice_b: If they weigh less than 50 pounds
choice_c: If they are stored in a locked metal box
choice_d: Explosives are never permitted in any part of the bus
explanation: The manual forbids explosives in the space occupied by people, except small arms ammunition.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: What quantity limits does the manual place on allowed hazardous materials a bus may carry?
choice_a: No more than 500 pounds total, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class
choice_b: No more than 250 pounds total, regardless of class
choice_c: Up to 1,000 pounds total, with no per-class limit
choice_d: No weight limit as long as materials are properly labeled
explanation: The manual forbids carrying more than 500 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: What is the purpose of the "standee line" on a bus designed to allow standing riders?
choice_a: It is a two-inch line showing riders they may not stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat
choice_b: It marks where wheelchair-accessible seating begins
choice_c: It shows where riders must stand while the bus is boarding
choice_d: It marks the location of the nearest emergency exit
explanation: The manual states no rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat, and buses designed to allow standing must have a two-inch line, called the standee line, that all standing riders must stay behind.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: When arriving at a destination or intermediate stop, which of the following should a driver announce?
choice_a: The location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number
choice_b: Only the bus number
choice_c: The driver's name and route history
choice_d: The weather forecast for the next stop
explanation: The manual lists the location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number as the items to announce when arriving at a destination or intermediate stop.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Why does the manual say charter bus drivers should not allow riders on the bus until departure time?
choice_a: To help prevent theft or vandalism of the bus
choice_b: To comply with a federal boarding-time law
choice_c: To allow time for a full vehicle inspection
choice_d: To ensure the bus is fully fueled first
explanation: The manual states that charter bus drivers should not allow riders on the bus until departure time, which helps prevent theft or vandalism of the bus.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: When is the best time for a driver to mention rules about smoking, drinking, or use of radios and tape players?
choice_a: At the start of the trip
choice_b: Only after a rider violates a rule
choice_c: At the midpoint of a long trip
choice_d: Only during the after-trip inspection
explanation: The manual advises mentioning rules about smoking, drinking, or use of radio and tape players at the start of the trip, since explaining rules early helps avoid trouble later.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Before starting a bus after riders have boarded or after a stop, what should a driver do to protect them?
choice_a: Wait for them to sit down or brace themselves
choice_b: Immediately accelerate to stay on schedule
choice_c: Sound the horn twice before moving
choice_d: Wait only until the doors are visibly closed
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to wait for riders to sit down or brace themselves before starting, and to make starts and stops as smooth as possible to avoid rider injury.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: Where does the manual suggest it may be safest to discharge a drunk or disruptive rider?
choice_a: At the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area where other people are present
choice_b: At the nearest railroad crossing
choice_c: Immediately, at the current location regardless of surroundings
choice_d: Only at the final destination of the route
explanation: The manual states a driver should not discharge such riders where it would be unsafe, and it may be safer at the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area where there are other people.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the Connecticut CDL manual, where do bus accidents most often happen?
choice_a: At intersections
choice_b: On drawbridges
choice_c: On banked curves
choice_d: At railroad crossings
explanation: The manual states that bus accidents often happen at intersections, and drivers should use caution even if a signal or stop sign controls other traffic.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: What does it mean if your bus leans toward the outside while on a banked curve?
choice_a: You are driving too fast
choice_b: The curve's design speed is too low
choice_c: The road surface has poor traction
choice_d: The bus is overloaded on one side
explanation: The manual states that if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, you are driving too fast, and speed should be reduced for curves.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: How far before a railroad crossing must a bus driver stop?
choice_a: Between 15 and 50 feet before the crossing
choice_b: Between 5 and 10 feet before the crossing
choice_c: At least 100 feet before the crossing
choice_d: Exactly 25 feet before the crossing
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop their bus between 15 and 50 feet before railroad crossings.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: If a bus has a manual transmission, what must the driver never do while crossing railroad tracks?
choice_a: Change gears
choice_b: Use the clutch to hold speed
choice_c: Sound the horn
choice_d: Open the forward door
explanation: The manual states that if your bus has a manual transmission, you should never change gears while crossing the tracks.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: At which of the following crossings does a bus driver NOT have to stop, though must still slow down and carefully check for other vehicles?
choice_a: A crossing marked "exempt" or "abandoned"
choice_b: Any crossing without gates
choice_c: Any crossing on a state highway
choice_d: A crossing with a malfunctioning signal
explanation: The manual lists crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned" among the situations where a driver does not have to stop but must slow down and carefully check for other vehicles.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: How far before an unsignaled, unattended drawbridge must a bus driver stop?
choice_a: At least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge
choice_b: At least 15 feet before the draw of the bridge
choice_c: At least 100 feet before the draw of the bridge
choice_d: Exactly at the foot of the bridge
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop at drawbridges that do not have a signal light or traffic control attendant, at least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

topic: Prohibited Practices - Fueling with Riders Aboard
question: What does the Connecticut CDL manual say about fueling a bus while riders are on board?
choice_a: Avoid it unless absolutely necessary, and never refuel in a closed building with riders aboard
choice_b: It is permitted at any time as long as the engine is off
choice_c: It is only prohibited in a closed building, regardless of necessity
choice_d: It is prohibited only if more than 10 riders are aboard
explanation: The manual states drivers should avoid fueling with riders on board unless absolutely necessary, and should never refuel in a closed building with riders on board.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-4

topic: Prohibited Practices - Towing or Pushing a Disabled Bus
question: When may a disabled bus be towed or pushed with riders still aboard?
choice_a: Only if getting off would be unsafe, and only to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers
choice_b: Whenever the distance to the next stop is less than one mile
choice_c: Never, under any circumstances
choice_d: Only with written permission from the DMV
explanation: The manual states drivers should not tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard unless getting off would be unsafe, and should only tow or push it to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-4

question: What does a bus's brake-door interlock system do?
choice_a: Applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open
choice_b: Locks the rear door until the parking brake is set
choice_c: Prevents the engine from starting until seatbelts are fastened
choice_d: Automatically shifts the transmission to neutral when a door opens
explanation: The manual explains that the interlock applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open, releasing when the rear door is closed; this feature should not be used in place of the parking brake.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-4
